semantic_fragments.content: The PEMS architecture specification makes use of and considers the following items to reduce RISK to an acceptable level where appropriate: (a) COMPONENTS WITH HIGH-INTEGRITY CHARACTERISTICS [N/A], (b) fail-safe functions [N/A], (c) redundancy [N/A], (d) diversity [N/A], (e) partitioning of functionality [P], (f) defensive design potentially limiting hazardous effects by restricting available output power or by introducing means to limit travel of actuators [N/A], (g) allocation of RISK CONTROL measures to subsystems and components of PEMS [N/A], (h) failure modes of components and their effects [P], (i) common cause failures [N/A], (j) systematic failures [P], (k) test interval duration and diagnostic coverage [P], (l) maintainability [N/A], (m) protection from reasonably foreseeable misuse [P], (n) IT-NETWORK specification, when applicable [N/A].

Under IEC60601-1 Clause 14.6.1, the MANUFACTURER must consider HAZARDS associated with both software and hardware aspects of PEMS, including hazards associated with incorporating PEMS into an IT-NETWORK, components of third-party origin, and legacy subsystems when compiling the list of known or foreseeable HAZARDS. Evidence provided in Risk Assessment Report, Edition 3.2-14.1 R50-R54.

The PEMS DEVELOPMENT LIFE-CYCLE problem resolution system documented in the Software Quality Plan (DN: PT9L-RJCH01 V1.0) meets all prescribed criteria: it is documented as part of PEMS DEVELOPMENT LIFE-CYCLE; it allows reporting of potential or existing problems affecting BASIC SAFETY or ESSENTIAL PERFORMANCE; it includes an assessment of each problem for associated RISKS; it identifies criteria that must be met for the issue to be closed; and it identifies the action to be taken to resolve each problem.
